root_cause.text: `intel_hdcp_gsc_check_status()` dereferenced `tile->media_gt` unconditionally and then accessed `gt->uc.gsc`, so when media GT was disabled and `media_gt` was NULL, the DRM HDCP/GSC status check triggered a NULL-pointer page fault.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!gt) { ... return false; }` before `gsc = &gt->uc.gsc;` and the commit message states that “when media GT is disabled via configfs, there is no allocation for media_gt, which is kept as NULL” and that `intel_hdcp_gsc_check_status()` “results in a kernel pagefault error due to gt->uc.gsc being evaluated as an invalid memory address.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: `intel_hdcp_gsc_check_status()` dereferenced `tile->media_gt` unconditionally and then accessed `gt->uc.gsc`, so when media GT was disabled and `media_gt` was NULL, the DRM HDCP/GSC status check triggered a NULL-pointer page fault.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (!gt) { ... return false; }` before `gsc = &gt->uc.gsc;` and the commit message states that “when media GT is disabled via configfs, there is no allocation for media_gt, which is kept as NULL” and that `intel_hdcp_gsc_check_status()` “results in a kernel pagefault error due to gt->uc.gsc being evaluated as an invalid memory address.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid null dereference by skipping HDCP2.x GSC status checks when the media GT is not present or disabled.
intent_record.what: The code now checks whether `gt` is null before accessing `gt->uc.gsc`, emits a debug message and returns false if the media GT is absent or disabled, and then assigns `gsc = &gt->uc.gsc` only after that check. It also removes the `!gsc` part of the later condition and now checks only `xe_uc_fw_is_available(&gsc->fw)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer dereferences `gt` when the media GT is unavailable, preventing a null-pointer access. If the media GT is missing or disabled, HDCP 2.x GSC status checking is skipped and reported as unavailable. The GSC firmware availability check remains, but assumes `gsc` is valid once `gt` is present.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid null dereference by skipping HDCP2.x GSC status checks when the media GT is not present or disabled.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by avoiding the NULL dereference in HDCP/GSC status checking when `media_gt` is absent or disabled, which matches the reported crash condition.

candidates.rationale: This dereferences tile->media_gt unconditionally. If media GT is disabled and the pointer is NULL, this line directly leads to a NULL-pointer dereference.
This accesses gt->uc.gsc after gt is obtained from tile->media_gt, so if gt is NULL the code faults here as part of the same unchecked dereference chain.
This check occurs too late to prevent the NULL dereference because gsc has already been derived from a potentially NULL gt; it is part of the vulnerable logic path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditionally dereferences tile->media_gt by assigning it to gt, and when media_gt is NULL the subsequent HDCP/GSC status path can fault.
This accesses gt->uc.gsc immediately after gt is taken from tile->media_gt, so if gt is NULL the code triggers the NULL-pointer dereference described in the root cause.
This guard is too late to prevent the crash because gsc has already been derived from a potentially NULL gt, so it participates in the vulnerable control flow.
